context:
Apart Research Swarm Alignment hackathon (tracks: Science of Agent Networks; Multi-Agent Oversight and Control). Deadline TONIGHT 2026-11-08 23:59 AoE; solo, AI-assisted; experiments must run in a few hours. Resources: Adaption API (hosted open-weight models: deepseek-v4-flash, qwen3.8-27b, gemma-4-31b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, glm-53-flash, glm-5.2, qwen3.5-397b; thousands of calls cost a few dollars); Modal (~$280, A100 for open-weight interpretability e.g. Gemma 4 31B); local 16 GB GPU.

RESEARCH OBJECTIVE: propose a RADICAL multi-agent ARCHITECTURE (information flow, roles, protocols, voting, memory, channels, incentives, or model-internal mechanism) under which LLM agent teams do NOT come to violate rules through social licensing, while still doing legitimate work. Each card is a testable hypothesis about one architecture: what it is, why it should work, what it predicts against a baseline, what result kills it, and a same-day experiment.

PILOT FINDINGS (Gemma 4 31B/26B; DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen never violated): a single agent with no history violates 0%; after seeing a rule-breaking proposal that 'passed' with silent peers, ~50%; unsigned peer hearsay ('the lead said it is fine') 33-50%; in live 4-agent teams with a shared log, one rule-citing reminder took 31B from 65% to 0% (26B barely moved); prior violations did NOT spread; teams were all-violate or all-comply from round 1. Prior art: Okamoto et al. 2608.12323 (peer outcomes/pressure break compliance across 12 models); Cerruti/Okamoto 2609.01836 (agent memory launders authorization); 2601.21112 (monitors with filtered information catch sabotage better, 'less is more'); CaMeL / dual-LLM (privileged vs quarantined LLM for prompt injection); 2607.29167 (provenance firewall for memory).

A test harness exists: actors + gate, worlds {none, passed proposal, unsigned hearsay, signed authorization}, measuring executed violations AND legitimate actions.
known_failure_modes: Unfalsifiable framing: a thesis where every outcome confirms it (e.g. 'context can override rules').
Bundled manipulations: a single contrast that cannot separate rival explanations (information vs permission vs detection vs wording vs length).
Circular interpretability: a direction built from the same contrast it is then used to explain or steer.
Probe reads the request/scenario, not the hidden variable (rule blindness, arXiv:2608.16852).
Decodable is not causal: steering vectors that predict but don't control; interchangeable vectors (arXiv:2610.19359).
Single-agent work relabelled as swarm research: 'peer' is just a string in one prompt.
Effect exists in few models (fine-as-price: 2 of 10 models in Wired Partners); 4B models may not show it.
Fine-tuning arms that cannot be done credibly in 1.5 days or whose result is already known (fine-tuning reroutes rather than rewrites).
Comparing effect sizes across studies with different models, tasks and baselines.
Claims of novelty for behaviour already published (Okamoto et al. arXiv:2608.12323; Wired Partners; Check Point Oct 2026; Shi et al. arXiv:2609.24967).
Punishment-vs-compensation (or any label) contrast as the key manipulation: a bundled wording change already covered by Okamoto and 'Same Odds, Different Deals'.
Severing all contact ends the whole repeated game (reputation, reciprocity, continuation value), so it cannot isolate one channel such as retaliation.
Retaliation that is only described in the prompt and never actually possible in the environment makes it a single-agent vignette.
Floor/ceiling effects: a predicted interaction that only exists because one cell is already near 0% or 100%.
Mediation claims resting on CoT mentions (CoT is often unfaithful) or on endogenous report/violation rates.

Novelty already covered: emergent whistleblowing in swarms (arXiv:2609.04170); anonymous reporting against retaliation (arXiv:2604.23511); eval/test-awareness probes and steering (arXiv:2505.14617, 2507.01786).
Scripted 'peers' that are just fixed transcripts shown to one focal agent: single-agent vignette, unless paired with a live-agent arm.
Silence or abstention that could mean 'detection is low' rather than 'norm accepted': designs must separate social inference from detection inference.
Prior art on silence/bystanders: Silence is Not Consensus (2505.21503), Silent Dissent (2610.02702), agent-bystander-study (Apart Oct 2026), Delegated Misalignment (EMNLP 2026).
Concept-fusion that only borrows vocabulary (e.g. calling a cascade an 'epidemic') without a distinct, testable prediction from the borrowed structure.
Refusal machine: an architecture that blocks violations by blocking everything; must report legitimate-action rate (signed authorization honored) alongside violation rate.
Renamed known defense: CaMeL/dual-LLM, constitutional classifiers, human-in-the-loop, monitor filtering (2601.21112), memory provenance firewalls (2607.29167) presented as new.
Architecture that only works because the base model is already compliant (DeepSeek/GLM/Qwen never violate); must be tested on susceptible actors (Gemma 4).
Untestable tonight: requires training a new model, human studies, or infrastructure that cannot be simulated with API agents in a few hours.
Laundering ignored: the actor can smuggle social claims into free-text justifications, tool arguments or memory; the design must say how it resists this.

cards.claim: [KILLED - negative example] Rules fall to quiet reframing, not to persuasion.
cards.mechanism: Argument triggers categorical defence; price mention silently switches mode.
cards.prediction: Argument lowers violations; fine mention raises them.
kill_reasons: Persuasive jailbreaks succeed >92% (Zeng et al. 2024); urgency pressure drives compliance to 0% in 10/12 models (Okamoto). Check Point backfire is one model, one scenario.
Built by comparing effect sizes across incomparable studies.

cards.claim: [KILLED - negative example] Fine-tuning a model to treat fines as prices causes broad emergent misalignment.
cards.mechanism: Narrow rule-breaking training generalizes via a persona direction.
kill_reasons: Standard template; Gemma shows ~0.7% EM; rational framing acts like inoculation; not credible in 1.5 days with one seed.

cards.claim: A norm firewall that separates the social channel (chat, proposals, hearsay) from the norm channel (rule plus signed authorization ledger), with a gate that sees only the rule, the ledger and the structured tool call, eliminates socially licensed violations without blocking signed legitimate actions.
cards.mechanism: Violations are licensed by social evidence in context; a gate that never reads social content cannot be licensed, while signed ledger entries still carry real permission. Free-text justifications are excluded because actors launder social claims into them.
cards.prediction: Executed violations: single agent ~50% after passed proposal; full-context gate similar; justification-reading gate intermediate; structured-only gate ~0%, with signed actions approved >=80%.
cards.falsifier: Structured-only gate still approves socially licensed actions >10%, or approves signed legitimate actions <60% (refusal machine), or the full-context gate already reaches ~0%.
cards.experiment: Gemma 4 31B and 26B actors; gate same model; 4 worlds x 4 architectures x 2 scenarios x 15 reps via Adaption API.
cards.swarm_link: Swarm governance by information-flow design: peers can share information but cannot move permissions; testable as a protocol for any agent network.
